text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The newly-estabilished Slovak Democratic Coalition (SDK), consisting of five main opposition parties, said it would initiate an extraordinary parliamentary session to demand the return of the parliamentary mandate to Jozef Gaulieder, who was expelled from parliament last December.

- The opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) said shortcomings in human rights and in the legal system as such would deteriorate if the ruling coalition ignores the Constitutional Court ruling demanding the return of Gaulieder's parliamentary mandate.
- The state-run Konsolidacna Banka said it would return by August 4 all funds collected within the scrapped import deposits scheme over the past two months.
- Recent floodings caused finacial damage on Slovak roads of around 219 million crowns.
SME - The government has asked Foreign Minister Zdenka Kramplova to proceed with diplomatic activities aimed at inviting NATO Secretary General Javier Solana to Slovakia later this year.

- Alcatel SEL THL, a Slovak subsidiary of the French telecomunications equipment producer Alcatel, will supply the state-run Slovak Telecom company with digital exchanges worth some 924 million crowns by the end of this year.

- The Slovak Chamber of Trade and Commerce has warned that the planned increase in energy prices for corporate customers would increase producer prices and endanger competetiveness of Slovak products.
PRAVDA - Only about 10 percent of the planned grain production was harvested by last weekend, but producers say harvesting works have been running on full steam since the beginning of this week.
- The opposition Democratic Union (DU) said it supported President Michal Kovac's proposal on early elections.
- The Slovak government will not hold its regular Tuesday session until August 12 due to the summer holiday.

- Bratislava District Prosecutor Michal Barila has begun investigation of allegations that Interior Minister Gustav Krajci deliberately thwarted the referendum on NATO membership and direct presidential elections last May. Barila said his office recieved "several tens" of appeals by citizens against Krajci's activities in the referendum.
